articles.title: The Exemption Card in the Chart Folder
articles.summary: A student who excels at chart work and has passed a fundamentals exemption test discovers during a comprehensive solo voyage that the deck basics long handled for him by the training division of labor are still part of what makes advanced navigation possible on his own.
articles.summaryZh: 一名海图成绩出色、且通过基础免修测试的学生，在综合单独航行中发现：被训练分工长期代办的甲板基础，仍是高阶航行能否独立完成的一环。
storyParagraphs: In the last comprehensive practical before the spring floods, Ji Heng had to deliver a cylinder of weather records to the outer-reef lighthouse before low tide, then return through the northern channel. Pass this test and he could still take a spring trainee berth on a merchant vessel; miss it, and he would wait another six months. Ji Heng’s chart work and tidal calculations had always been the best in the class. On admission, he brought a deck-completion record from his former sailing school and, in front of the instructor, tied the required knot correctly three times in a row with a practice rope. On that evidence, the school exempted him from the month-long deck fundamentals course. From then on, the exemption card stayed tucked inside the chart folder he used most.

For the next few weeks, the exemption seemed to carry no cost at all. Navigation training was divided by role: the duty sailors prepared the mooring lines, sheets, and hoisting lines, while the students judged wind, tide, and route. Twice Ji Heng altered course for a cross-current and reached the marker ahead of the others in his group. Once, during a sail change, a loose rope end was casually retied by a sailor while Ji Heng looked down to check his position; another time, before a lamp was hoisted, a sailor tightened the loaded knot first. The ropes Ji Heng took over were always already ready to work. The exemption card in his chart folder looked more and more like proof that the decision had been right.

The comprehensive practical had different rules: from departure to return, the student had to handle everything alone, and shore staff were not allowed to touch the ropes for him. The forecast clearly said the crosswind would strengthen after ten, and Ji Heng had already marked “reef before the red buoy” on his route. The first half went exactly to plan. At the red buoy, wearing wet gloves, he wrapped the damp sheet around the cleat and tied the same knot he had used in his entrance test. As soon as the sail came under load again, the rope end slowly slipped back half a finger-width. He untied it and tried again. At rest it looked neat; under load it began to slide once more. The line on the chart was correct, but the sail he had failed to shorten was pushing the bow toward the pale water over the shallows.

Ji Heng first pinned the rope end with the heel of his hand, still trying to get the record cylinder to the lighthouse. But the moment he released it to reach for the hoisting line, the rope slid farther and the boat swung broadside; another examination boat was approaching behind him along the same safe line. He shoved the cylinder back into the cabin, turned the helm into the wind, and raised the return flag. By the time he reached harbor, his tide window had passed. The test was recorded as incomplete, and the spring trainee berth went to the reserve student. The instructor did not change the equipment. Using Ji Heng’s same wet rope and the same cleat, he tied the knot and had three people pull backward together; it did not move. Then he asked Ji Heng to tie it once more on an unloaded rope. Ji Heng still performed every step correctly.

Ji Heng did not redraw his charts or do more paper exercises. He took the exemption card out and carried it, together with his charts, into the ground-floor deck room. For the next four weeks, he practiced first with dry rope, then with wet rope, thick gloves, and different directions of load. Sometimes the instructor put the sail under tension first and only then told him which knot to change to; sometimes he made Ji Heng switch continuously among reefing, mooring, and hoisting a lamp. When Ji Heng moved too slowly, the rope immediately bit into his glove. When he chose poorly, the model boat drifted off its marked line. More than once, the bell for the chart class upstairs had already rung while he was still untying the knot he had just made and starting again under a different condition.

The second practical again followed the outer reef, and the forecast crosswind was stronger than before. Before the red buoy, Ji Heng reefed the sail; once the wet rope took the load, it stayed where he had set it. Near the lighthouse, he changed hands to reach for the hoisting line, and the rope end on the cleat did not move. When he signed back in at harbor, a new passing stamp was pressed onto the inside cover of his chart folder. Ji Heng folded the old exemption card into a narrow strip and wrapped it around the rolled chart. Then, with the rope he had just taken off the deck, he tied the two together.
storyParagraphsZh: 春汛前最后一次综合实操，季衡要在退潮前把一筒气象记录送到外礁灯塔，再沿北侧水道返回。通过这次考核，他就能赶上商船的春季见习位；错过，要再等半年。季衡的海图和潮汐计算一直是全班最好。入学时，他拿着旧帆校的甲板结业记录，又在教员面前用练习绳连续三次系对规定绳结。凭这两项证据，学校准许他免修一个月的甲板基础课。那张免修卡，从此一直夹在他最常用的海图夹里。
之后几周，免修看不出任何代价。导航训练本来就按岗位分工：值班水手先把靠泊绳、缭绳和吊索理到位，学员负责判断风、潮和航线。季衡两次根据横流改线，都比同组的人更早到标记点。一次换帆时，一根绳头松了，水手在他低头核对方位时顺手重系；另一次吊灯前，水手先把受力的绳结压紧。季衡接过来的，总是已经能工作的绳。海图夹里的免修卡越来越像一张正确的证明。
综合实操的规则不同：学生从离岸到返港都要独立操作，岸上人员不得替他碰绳。当天预报写明十点后侧风会增强，季衡也把“红浮标前缩帆”画进了自己的路线。前半程一切照计划进行。到红浮标时，他戴着湿手套，把受潮的缭绳绕上羊角桩，系出自己在入学测试里做过的那个结。帆一重新受力，绳头却缓慢退出半指；他解开重系，静止时仍整齐，一吃力又开始滑。海图上的线没错，船头却被没有收住的帆推向浅色水面。
季衡先用掌根压住绳头，仍想把记录筒送上灯塔。可他一松手去取吊索，绳又滑出一截，船身随即横过去；后方另一艘考核艇正按同一条安全线接近。他把记录筒塞回舱内，转舵迎风，升起返航旗。返港后，他的潮窗已经过去，考核记为未完成，春季见习位由候补学生补上。教员没有换器材，就用季衡那根湿绳、同一只羊角桩系好，让三个人一起向后拉；绳结没有移动。随后让季衡在不受力的绳上再系一次，他仍能完整做对。
季衡没有重画海图，也没有再做更多纸面题。他把免修卡抽出来，连同海图一起带进一楼甲板室。接下来的四周，他先在干绳上练，再换湿绳、厚手套和不同受力方向；有时教员先让帆吃上力，再临时指定他改结，有时让他在收帆、靠泊和吊灯之间连续切换。动作慢时，绳会立刻把手套勒紧；选错时，船模会偏离标线。几次楼上海图课的钟已经响了，他仍把刚系好的结拆开，换一种条件重来。
第二次实操仍走外礁，预报中的侧风比上次更硬。到红浮标前，季衡先缩帆，湿绳受力后停在原处；靠近灯塔时，他换手去接吊索，羊角桩上的绳头也没有动。返航登记时，新的合格章盖在海图夹内页。季衡把旧免修卡折成一条窄带，绕住卷起的海图，最后用那根刚从甲板上解下来的绳，把两样东西系在一起。
explanationParagraphs: A prerequisite structure means that complex learning depends on foundational components that can be called upon reliably. Advanced performance can sometimes appear successful because other people, tools, or familiar conditions quietly fill a gap. It does not require everyone to follow exactly the same sequence, but when a later task genuinely depends on a foundation, the learner must be able to use it independently.
explanationParagraphsZh: 先备知识结构指复杂学习依赖若干能被稳定调用的基础成分。高阶表现有时看似成立，只因他人、工具或熟悉环境暗中补上了缺口。它并不要求所有人遵循完全相同的顺序，但当后续任务真正需要某项基础时，学习者必须能够独立使用它。

module.intro: Advanced tasks often require more than having used a basic skill once; they require those foundations to be available on demand under real conditions.
module.diagramTitle: From a Gap Hidden by Support to Independent Performance
diagramSteps: Identify the foundational components required by the complex task
Show advanced performance in an environment with support
Remove the support and expose an unstable foundation
Rebuild and reintegrate the foundation under varied conditions
Test independent stability through the complete task
diagramStepNotes: First ask which capabilities the final task actually requires at the same time.
Strong results may partly come from other people preparing things in advance, tool prompts, or familiar conditions.
A hidden gap enters the task outcome only when the learner must perform independently.
Remedial practice should not only repeat a standard example, but also cover changes in load, wetness, time pressure, and other conditions.
The final check should return to the whole task rather than looking only at whether a single drill has been passed.
mapping: Leading scores in chart work and tidal calculation → The advanced component itself is not the source of the problem
Duty sailors prepare the ropes in advance → External support has long substituted for part of the foundational performance
Wet rope under load in the solo practical → Once the support is removed, the foundational gap directly changes the course of the boat
Retie knots under varied conditions → “Knowing how” becomes a skill that can be called upon reliably
The exemption card and chart are tied together with the same rope → The foundation and the advanced skill were always part of the same capability chain
module.boundary: A prerequisite structure does not mean that everyone must learn through the same course sequence, nor does it mean that every mistake comes from a missing foundation. If a learner can already perform the foundational component reliably under the target conditions, a justified exemption can still be appropriate; the key question is whether the capabilities required by the final task are genuinely available.
module.reflection: If someone always prepared the ropes before Ji Heng’s navigation practice, which of his results could not actually prove that he could complete the whole task independently?

moduleZh.intro: 高阶任务常常不是把基础能力“用过一次”就够了，而是要求它们在真实条件下随时可被调用。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 从被支架遮住的缺口到独立完成
diagramSteps: 明确复杂任务需要的基础成分
在有支架的环境中出现高阶表现
撤去支架并暴露不稳定的基础能力
在变化条件下补齐并重新整合
用完整任务检验独立稳定性
diagramStepNotes: 先问最终任务实际要同时调用哪些能力。
好成绩可能部分来自他人预先处理、工具提示或熟悉条件。
只有必须独立完成时，隐藏缺口才会真正进入任务结果。
补练不只重复标准样例，还要覆盖受力、湿滑、时间压力等变化。
最终要回到完整任务，而不是只看单项练习是否通过。
mapping: 海图与潮汐成绩领先 → 高阶部分本身并非问题来源
值班水手预先理绳 → 外部支架长期替代了部分基础调用
单独实操中的湿绳受力 → 支架撤走后基础缺口直接改变航线
变化条件下重新练结 → 把“会做”提升为可稳定调用
免修卡与海图被同一根绳系住 → 基础与高阶原本属于同一条能力链
moduleZh.boundary: 先备结构不等于所有人必须按同一课程顺序学习，也不意味着一次失误都源于基础不足。若学习者已经能在目标条件下稳定完成基础环节，合理免修仍然成立；关键是最终任务所需能力是否真实可用。
moduleZh.reflection: 如果季衡在导航训练中始终有人先把绳理好，哪些成绩其实无法证明他已经能独立完成整项任务？

articles.title: Twenty-Eight Seconds
articles.summary: Before a new café opens, A-Lan moves into a more complex multi-order task after a single apparently successful attempt because everyone follows the same training timetable. By separating the task and gathering repeated evidence, the trainer later pinpoints a tamping gap; only after targeted correction and repeated checks against the original standard does A-Lan continue to the next stage of training.
articles.summaryZh: 新咖啡店开业前，阿岚因统一训练时刻表在一次表面合格后进入更复杂的连单任务，随后用拆分任务与重复证据定位压粉缺口，经过针对性纠正并按原标准反复验证后才继续后续训练。
storyParagraphs: The new café was due to open on Saturday, and A-Lan had been assigned the first morning shift. What worried her most was not whether her latte art looked beautiful, but whether, at 7:30, when the first wave of commuters came in from the metro station, she could get the cups out one by one on time. On Thursday morning, four new employees began two days of training: espresso at nine, milk steaming at eleven, consecutive orders in the afternoon, then a full simulation the next day. The shop had only one training espresso machine and one grinder, and coffee beans and milk were prepared by time slot, so whenever the timer on the wall rang, everyone moved to the next task. That way, no one occupied the equipment for too long, and the manager could still schedule Saturday's shifts as planned.

During the morning single-shot check, A-Lan weighed out 18 grams of coffee, tamped it, locked in the portafilter, and started the timer. At 27.8 seconds, 36 grams of espresso had reached the cup, and the taste showed no obvious problem. It sat neatly within the standard of 26 to 30 seconds and 36 grams, plus or minus 2 grams. Mei put a check mark on the form. But as A-Lan rinsed the portafilter, she noticed that the edge of the coffee puck was uneven in depth. She could not explain why, so she weighed another 18 grams and prepared to pull a second shot immediately to check. Then the eleven o'clock bell rang. According to the training schedule, espresso practice was over, and all four moved on to milk steaming. The coffee she had already weighed had to be tipped into the waste bin.

The problem properly surfaced that afternoon when they practised making two drinks in sequence. A-Lan steamed the milk first, then prepared two espressos one after the other: one ran through in 23 seconds, while the other dragged on to 33, and the milk foam she had made first slowly coarsened while she waited. Mei did not ask her to repeat the whole routine, nor did she adjust the machine first. Instead, she had a colleague take over the milk pitcher, leaving A-Lan only the dosing, distribution, and tamping; the grinder setting, the 18-gram dose, and the training machine all remained unchanged. Her colleague produced an espresso within range on the same equipment. When A-Lan tried again, the flow still began from the right side of the portafilter. With a bottomless portafilter fitted, two consecutive shots again started on the right; when the basket was removed, the tamped coffee bed was also lower on the right both times. Even after the multitasking had been taken away, the same deviation remained.

Under the original timetable, the other three had already moved on to practising heart-shaped latte art. Mei kept A-Lan at the espresso station and changed only one action. She placed a small strip of white tape on the right side of the portafilter so that, after tamping, A-Lan would check the height all the way around the basket; she kept her wrist straight and moved her elbow directly above the portafilter. For the first three attempts, she practised only making the surface level, without using the machine. The fourth extraction took 31.4 seconds and still failed the standard. A-Lan shifted her stance half a step to the left and tried again: 28.9 seconds, then 28.1 seconds. Both shots were judged against exactly the same morning standard. She was not given an extra second, nor was a gram taken away.

As a result, she began latte-art practice more than twenty minutes later than the other three and used several extra portions of coffee beans. When she returned to the consecutive-order exercise that afternoon, Mei handed the milk pitcher back to her. The two espressos finished at 28.3 and 27.9 seconds. The flow no longer pulled to the right, and the milk foam no longer coarsened while she waited. Only then did Mei add the date beside the morning check mark and let her move on to the full simulation the next day. The bell on the wall continued to ring on schedule; it simply no longer decided whether this particular action was stable enough.

At 7:30 on Saturday morning, the first ticket slid out of the printer: two lattes and one flat white. A-Lan weighed the coffee, tamped it level, locked in the portafilter, then reached for the milk pitcher. As the steam began to hiss, she glanced sideways at the timer. Dark coffee fell evenly from the bottom of the portafilter, and the number stopped at 28.4 seconds.
storyParagraphsZh: 周六新咖啡店就要开门，阿岚被排在清晨第一班。她最担心的不是拉花漂不漂亮，而是七点半地铁口第一拨客人同时进来时，自己能不能把杯子一杯杯准时送出去。周四早上，四名新员工开始两天训练：九点练浓缩，十一点练奶泡，下午练连续出单，第二天做整套模拟。店里只有一台训练机，磨豆机也只有一台，咖啡豆和牛奶按时段备好，所以墙上的计时铃一响，所有人就换到下一项。这样没人长期占住设备，店长也能按计划安排周六班次。
上午的单杯检查，阿岚称了十八克咖啡粉，压粉、扣上手柄，按下计时。二十七点八秒，杯里落下三十六克浓缩，味道也没有明显问题，正好落在二十六到三十秒、三十六克上下两克的标准里。梅姐在表格上画了一个勾。阿岚冲洗手柄时，却看见粉饼边缘深浅不太一样。她说不上原因，便又称好十八克，准备马上做第二杯确认。十一点铃响，按训练表浓缩练习结束，四个人一起转去奶泡。那份已经称好的粉只好倒进废粉盒。

下午练两杯连做，问题才真正露出来。阿岚先打奶，再连续准备两份浓缩：一杯二十三秒就流完，另一杯拖到三十三秒，先打好的奶泡在等待里慢慢变粗。梅姐没有让她把整套流程重做，也没有先调机器，而是让同伴接手奶缸，只留下称粉、布粉和压粉；磨豆刻度、十八克粉量和那台训练机都不变。同伴用同一套设备做出的浓缩落在范围内，阿岚再做时，细流仍总从手柄右侧先落下。换上能看见萃取底部的手柄，连续两次都向右先出液；拆下粉碗，压过的粉面也连续两次右侧偏低。多任务被拿掉后，同一个偏差还在。
按原来的时刻表，其他三个人已经去练心形拉花。梅姐把阿岚留在浓缩台旁，只改一个动作：在手柄右侧贴一小段白胶带，让她压完后沿粉碗看一圈高度，手腕放直，肘部移到手柄正上方。前三次只练压平，不上机；第四次萃取用了三十一点四秒，仍不合格。阿岚把站姿向左挪了半步，再做一杯二十八点九秒，又一杯二十八点一秒；两杯都仍按上午同一条标准判断，没有多给一秒，也没有少要一克。
她因此比另外三个人晚了二十多分钟进入拉花练习，也多用了几份咖啡豆。下午重新做连单时，梅姐把奶缸重新交还给她。两杯浓缩分别在二十八点三秒和二十七点九秒结束，粉流没有再偏向右侧，奶泡也没有因等待变粗。到这时，梅姐才在上午那个勾旁补上日期，让她进入第二天的整套模拟。墙上的铃仍照常响，只是不再替她决定这个动作是否已经学稳。
周六七点半，第一张小票从机器里吐出来：两杯拿铁，一杯馥芮白。阿岚称粉，压平，扣上手柄，再去拿奶缸。蒸汽声起来时，她侧头看了一眼计时器。深色咖啡从手柄底部均匀落下，数字停在二十八点四秒。
explanationParagraphs: Mastery learning begins by defining goals clearly enough to be tested, then using formative evidence to identify specific gaps. Learners do not automatically move to the next stage simply because they have spent the same amount of time. When a gap appears, targeted correction, feedback, and another attempt can be provided, and progression follows after the same standard has been met. Holding the standard constant does not require every learner to take the same amount of time or follow exactly the same path.

This approach does not mean extending learning time without limit or lowering expectations. Bloom (1968) emphasized explicit mastery, quality of instruction, perseverance, and the time allowed for learning. Bloom (1984) discussed mastery learning, tutoring, time on task, corrective feedback, and other alterable factors; its well-known historical effect estimates should not be treated as universal guarantees. Kulik, Kulik, and Bangert-Drowns (1990), in a meta-analysis of 108 controlled evaluations, reported generally positive but variable results, while also noting that mastery approaches may increase learning time and, in some self-paced college programs, may carry completion-rate costs.
explanationParagraphsZh: 掌握学习强调先把目标定义得清楚、可检验，再依据形成性证据判断具体缺口。学习者不因相同课时自动进入下一阶段；发现缺口后，可以采用针对性纠正、反馈和再次尝试，达到同一标准后再继续。相同标准并不要求所有人用相同时间或完全相同的学习路径。

这一思路并不等于无限延长学习时间或降低要求。Bloom 1968 强调明确掌握、教学质量、坚持与允许的学习时间；Bloom 1984 讨论了掌握学习、辅导、任务时间、纠正性反馈等可改变因素，其中著名的历史效应估计不应被当作普遍保证。Kulik、Kulik 与 Bangert-Drowns 1990 对108项对照评估的元分析报告总体积极但有差异的结果，也指出学习时间可能增加，并在部分自定进度大学项目中出现完成率成本。

module.intro: This module helps readers see that a learning problem does not necessarily come from a learner's lack of ability. It may arise because a common pace carries one unstable action into a more complex task. The key is not simply to add more practice, but to use evidence to locate the gap, correct it specifically, and then verify performance again against the original standard.
module.diagramTitle: From Common Pace to Mastery-Based Progression
diagramSteps: Shared goal
Identify the gap
Targeted correction
Try again
Meet the standard, then progress
diagramStepNotes: Define a clear, testable goal and standard first.
Use formative evidence to identify the specific element that is not yet stable.
Adjust support or practice only for the gap that has been identified.
Try again under the same standard and receive feedback.
Move into the more complex next task only after the standard has been met.
mapping: The eleven o'clock bell and the single training machine → The common timetable has a real resource rationale, but it also moves everyone to the next task at the same time.

The 27.8-second, 36-gram single shot and the second check interrupted by the bell → One apparently successful attempt does not show whether the action is stable, and the fixed pace lets an unverified gap move forward.

Flow starting on the same side, the lower right side of the coffee bed, and the same pattern remaining after milk steaming is removed → Formative evidence narrows the problem from 'struggling with consecutive orders' to the tamping action.

The white tape, straight wrist, repositioned elbow, and the first three repetitions devoted only to levelling the coffee bed → Correction is aimed at one identified gap rather than mechanically repeating the entire routine.

28.9 and 28.1 seconds, followed by 28.3 and 27.9 seconds during consecutive orders → Performance is repeatedly checked against the same morning standard, and only then does A-Lan return to latte art and the full simulation.
module.boundary: Mastery learning is most applicable when goals can be reasonably defined, observed, and tested, and when there is some room for additional time and support. It does not mean that everyone must achieve identical outcomes, nor does it mean unlimited extensions, lower standards, or repeatedly doing the same task. In practice, targeted support can add time, material, and organizational costs. Research findings are generally positive but vary across programs, subjects, and study designs, and some self-paced settings may face completion-rate costs. The historical effect estimates reported in Bloom (1984) should not be treated as universal guarantees.
module.reflection: If the eleven o'clock bell had not rung, what might A-Lan's second 18-gram dose have changed?

moduleZh.intro: 这个模块帮助读者看见：问题不一定来自学习者能力不足，而可能来自统一进度把一个尚未稳定的具体动作带进了更复杂任务。关键不是简单增加练习次数，而是先用证据定位缺口，再针对纠正，并用原来的标准重新验证。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 从统一进度到达标前进
diagramSteps: 共同目标
发现缺口
针对纠正
再次尝试
达标前进
diagramStepNotes: 先把可检验的目标和标准说清楚。
用形成性证据找出尚未稳定的具体环节。
只针对已识别的缺口调整支持或练习。
在相同标准下重新尝试并获得反馈。
达到标准后再进入更复杂的后续任务。
mapping: 十一点计时铃与唯一训练机 → 统一时刻表有真实资源理由，也会把所有人同时推向下一项。
27.8秒、36克的单杯与被铃声打断的第二次确认 → 一次表面合格没有暴露动作是否稳定，固定进度使未确认的缺口继续向前。
同侧先出液、右侧粉面偏低以及拿掉奶泡后的重复出现 → 形成性证据把问题从“连单做不好”缩小到压粉动作。
白胶带、手腕放直、肘部移正与前三次只练压平 → 纠正只针对已定位的一个缺口，而不是把整套流程机械重做。
28.9、28.1以及连单中的28.3、27.9秒 → 使用上午同一标准重复验证，达标后才恢复拉花和整套模拟。
moduleZh.boundary: 掌握学习适合目标能够被合理定义、观察和检验，并且有一定时间与支持空间的情境。它不意味着所有人都必须得到完全相同结果，也不意味着无限延时、降低标准或反复做同一任务。现实中，针对性支持会增加时间、材料与组织成本；研究结果总体积极但会随程序、学科和研究设计而变化，部分自定进度情境还可能面临完成率成本。Bloom 1984 的历史效应估计也不能当作普遍保证。
moduleZh.reflection: 如果十一点的铃没有响，阿岚手里那第二份十八克咖啡粉可能会改变什么？

references.citation: Bloom, B. S. (1968). Learning for Mastery. Evaluation Comment, 1(2), 1–12.
references.use: Foundational statement of learning for mastery; treats aptitude partly as time required and stresses quality of instruction, perseverance, time allowed, and explicit mastery.

references.citation: Bloom, B. S. (1984). The 2 Sigma Problem: The Search for Methods of Group Instruction as Effective as One-to-One Tutoring. Educational Researcher, 13(6), 4–16.
references.use: Examines mastery learning, tutoring, time on task, corrective feedback, and alterable educational variables; its famous effect estimates should be presented as historical findings, not universal guarantees.

references.citation: Kulik, C.-L. C., Kulik, J. A., & Bangert-Drowns, R. L. (1990). Effectiveness of Mastery Learning Programs: A Meta-Analysis. Review of Educational Research, 60(2), 265–299.
references.use: Meta-analysis of 108 controlled evaluations; reports generally positive but variable effects, increased time on task, and possible completion-rate costs in self-paced college programs.

articles.title: After the Timer Rang
articles.summary: On the morning a new bakery opens, a pastry chef follows the reliable twenty-minute rhythm she learned in a stable kitchen, only to discover that the same amount of time no longer means the same state under different temperatures and equipment conditions.
articles.summaryZh: 新店开业早晨，一名西点师沿用在稳定厨房里可靠的二十分钟节奏，却逐渐发现同样的时间在新的温度与设备条件下已不再代表同样的面团状态。
storyParagraphs: At six on Saturday morning, the lights were already on in the new bakery on the corner. Lin Qiao had to deliver ninety croissants by eight for the café next door to serve at its opening breakfast. She had spent three years working in a hotel pastry kitchen. The laminating room there stayed at eighteen degrees, the refrigerator held only dough and butter, and after each fold the dough rested for twenty minutes; when it came out, dough and butter were usually soft enough to bend together without leaking. She had followed that rhythm hundreds of times. The first round in the new shop went smoothly too. When the timer rang, the edges of the dough were neat and the butter had not broken through.

After half past six, the ovens began warming the room, deliveries started coming through the front door, and cream, milk, and fruit were added to the refrigerator. After the second twenty-minute rest, the dough felt a little softer than it had at the hotel, but it still rolled out cleanly, and a small trimmed piece puffed into visible layers in the test oven. With more than an hour left before delivery, the owner went out front to arrange the cups, and Lin Qiao continued with the familiar rhythm for the third round. At that point, there was no clear reason to disrupt the whole batch because of one uncertain difference in feel.

When the timer rang for the third time, she opened the refrigerator but did not take the dough out at once. The edge of the paper around the butter had softened. She pressed the dough with the back of a finger, then the butter sheet: one still had some resistance, while the other yielded quickly. She set them side by side on the counter for five minutes, and the difference became clearer. The wall thermometer read twenty-six degrees, and the refrigerator door had been opened several times for milk. Lin Qiao reset the phone for twenty minutes, but did not press start. She pushed this batch back into the refrigerator and decided that from then on she would first check whether dough and butter could bend with similar firmness without becoming soft, and only then decide when to roll.

Meanwhile, the earlier batch at the other end of the counter had already been shaped and placed in the proofing cabinet. Fifteen minutes later, the tips of several pieces began to sag, and butter seeped from the lower edges, gathering in bright circles on the trays. In the end, thirty-six could not be delivered. The café staff arrived at the door pushing an empty insulated box, and Lin Qiao could only send over part of the acceptable batch, promise the rest forty minutes late, and waive part of the charge. The owner moved the order clip marked “90” from the doorway to the till, but did not urge her to rush the remaining dough through in the old way.

Lin Qiao divided the remaining dough into smaller portions, used ice water for the next mix, and chilled the butter sheets in advance. From then on, after each rest she snapped off a small corner, felt the resistance of the dough, and lightly pressed the butter: if they were too firm, she waited longer; if they began softening too quickly, she took them out sooner. The timer now only reminded her to check; it no longer made the decision for her. When the first small tray came out of the oven, there were no rings of butter around the edges, and when she cut one open, the layers had lifted into separate pockets. She continued the same way. It was slower, but she did not lose another whole tray.

At 8:47, the last insulated box reached the café next door. Early the next morning, Lin Qiao set her phone for twenty minutes again. When the alarm sounded, she opened the refrigerator, pressed the dough with the back of a finger, touched the butter, and closed the door again. Seven minutes later, she finally took the tray out. The phone screen was still showing “00:00”.
storyParagraphsZh: 周六早上六点，街角新开的面包房已经亮灯。林乔要在八点前交出九十只羊角包，供隔壁咖啡馆做开业早餐。她在酒店西点房做了三年：折叠间常年十八度，冷柜只放面团和黄油，折好后冷藏二十分钟，出柜时两样东西通常都能一起弯、又不会渗油。这个节奏她做过上百次。新店第一轮也很顺，计时器一响，面团边角齐整，黄油没有破。
六点半以后，烤箱陆续升温，前门开始进货，冷柜里多了奶油、牛奶和水果。第二轮二十分钟后，面团比酒店里软一点，但擀开仍然干净，一块切下来的边角料进小烤箱后也鼓出了层次。离交货还有一个多小时，老板去前厅摆杯子，林乔继续按原来的节奏做第三轮；眼下没有理由为了一个不确定的手感打乱整批进度。
第三次铃声响时，她拉开冷柜，却没有马上把面团端走。包黄油的纸边已经发软，她用指背压了压面团，又压了压黄油片：一个还带着韧劲，一个却很快陷下去。她把两样东西并排放了五分钟，差别更明显。墙上的温度计指着二十六度，冷柜门又因取牛奶开合了几次。林乔把手机重新设到二十分钟，却没有按开始；她先把这一批推回冷柜，决定以后先看两者能不能以相近的软硬一起弯，再决定什么时候擀。
这时，案台另一端那批较早开始、已经整形好的生坯进了醒发箱。十五分钟后，几只尖角开始塌，黄油从底边渗出来，在烤盘上聚成亮圈。三十六只最后没能交货，咖啡馆的人推着空保温箱等在门口，林乔只能先送出合格的一部分，并答应晚四十分钟补齐，还免掉了一部分货款。老板把写着“90”的订单夹从门口移到收银台，没有催她把剩下的面团照旧赶完。
林乔把剩下的面团分成小份，用冰水和下一盆，黄油片提前冷好。之后每次冷藏，她都先掰一小角，摸面团的韧劲，再轻压黄油：太硬就多等，开始发软就提前收回；计时器只负责提醒她去看，不再替她决定。第一小盘出炉时，底边没有油圈，切开后能看见层层撑起的空隙。她照这个办法继续，速度慢了些，却没有再出现整盘报废。
八点四十七分，最后一个保温箱送到隔壁。第二天清晨，林乔又把手机设成二十分钟。铃声响起时，她拉开冷柜，用指背压了压面团，又碰了碰黄油，随即把门重新关上。七分钟后，她才把那一盘端出来；手机屏幕还停在“00:00”。
explanationParagraphs: Transfer of learning means using knowledge or skills gained in one situation in a different situation. Effective transfer is not the mechanical repetition of familiar steps. It requires identifying which underlying principles or relationships from earlier experience still hold, then adapting the action to cues in the new context. Differences in content, physical setting, time, and social context can all affect transfer distance, so near and far transfer should not be treated as one single, fixed effect.

Transfer is also not only about whether someone can immediately reproduce an old answer. A new situation may require the learner to identify available resources, notice what information is still missing, ask better questions, and keep learning and adapting through feedback. Looking at whether learners are prepared for future learning therefore broadens transfer beyond one-time reproduction of previous performance.
explanationParagraphsZh: 学习迁移指把一种情境中获得的知识或技能用于不同情境。有效迁移不是机械复现熟悉步骤，而是识别旧经验中仍成立的原理或关系，再依据新情境线索调整做法。内容、物理环境、时间、社会情境等方面的差异都会影响迁移距离，因此近迁移与远迁移不能被理解为单一、固定的效果。
迁移也不只看一个人能否立即复现旧答案。新的情境可能要求先识别可用资源、发现需要补充的信息、提出更好的问题，并利用反馈继续学习和适应。把学习者是否为后续学习做好准备纳入考察，可以看到迁移还包括在变化中继续学习，而不只是一次性复制既有表现。

module.intro: This module helps readers distinguish between remembering a set of steps and carrying what is genuinely useful into a new situation. Lin Qiao does not abandon her previous experience. Instead, she reconsiders which part of that experience still holds and which part was only a reliable time signal under stable conditions, then uses feedback from the new environment to adjust what she does.
module.diagramTitle: From Repeating Steps to Adapting to a New Context
diagramSteps: Old context
Extract the principle
Identify new conditions
Adapt the application
Use outcome feedback
diagramStepNotes: In the hotel's stable temperature and dedicated refrigerator, twenty minutes usually produced a state suitable for the next fold.
What needs to carry over is not the fixed number of minutes, but the relative state in which dough and butter can bend together without becoming too soft or leaking.
The warmer new shop, shared refrigerator, and frequent door opening mean that the same twenty minutes no longer reliably produce the old state.
Lin Qiao turns the timer into a reminder to inspect, checking dough and butter first before deciding whether to keep chilling or start rolling.
Losses from the earlier batch reveal the risk, while the adjusted small tray and later croissants provide new feedback.
mapping: The “twenty-minute” timer → a reliable surface cue in the old environment, but not a rule that remains valid across all contexts.

An eighteen-degree laminating room versus a twenty-six-degree new shop, and a dedicated refrigerator versus a shared one → contextual differences change the relationship between the old procedure and its result.
Pressing the dough and butter side by side → a shift from copying a timed step to judging the relative state the two materials need to reach.
Using the timer only as a reminder while making the actual chilling time longer or shorter → adapting the old method to new conditions rather than discarding prior experience altogether.
Thirty-six discarded croissants and the restored layers in the adjusted small tray → outcome feedback used to test and continue refining the new judgment.
module.boundary: Transfer has something to build on only when the new task shares some structure with the old one. In near transfer, where content and context differ less, old cues are more likely to remain useful. In far transfer, or when transfer distance is greater, surface similarities may mislead, so learners need to extract principles, identify resources, ask questions, and experiment more actively. Transfer is not automatic, and one success or failure should not be generalized to every situation.
module.reflection: Which fixed step I rely on now is actually only a proxy signal from an old environment? In a new context, what should I observe first?

moduleZh.intro: 这个模块帮助读者区分“记住一套步骤”和“把真正有用的东西带到新情境”。林乔没有抛弃旧经验，而是重新判断旧经验里什么仍然成立、什么只是稳定环境下可靠的时间信号，再用新环境的反馈修正做法。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 从照搬步骤到适应新情境
diagramSteps: 旧情境
抽取原理
识别新条件
调整应用
结果反馈
diagramStepNotes: 在酒店的稳定温度和专用冷柜中，二十分钟通常能带来适合继续折叠的状态。
真正需要保留的不是固定分钟数，而是让面团与黄油达到能够一起弯曲、又不过软渗油的相对状态。
新店升温、冷柜混放且频繁开门，使同样二十分钟不再稳定地产生原来的状态。
林乔把计时器改成提醒工具，先检查面团和黄油，再决定继续冷藏还是开始擀制。
旧批次的损失暴露风险，调整后的第一小盘和后续成品则提供了新的反馈。
mapping: “二十分钟”计时器 → 旧环境中可靠的表面线索，但不是跨情境都成立的规则。
十八度折叠间与二十六度新店、专用冷柜与混用冷柜 → 情境差异改变了原做法与结果之间的关系。
并排按压面团和黄油 → 从复制时间步骤转向判断两者应达到的相对状态。
计时器只提醒检查、实际冷藏可延长或缩短 → 根据新条件调整原有做法，而不是完全丢弃旧经验。
三十六只报废与调整后小盘重新起层 → 结果反馈用来检验并继续修正判断。
moduleZh.boundary: 当新任务与旧任务共享一定结构时，迁移才有可利用的基础。近迁移中，内容和情境差异较小，旧线索往往更容易继续有效；远迁移或迁移距离较大时，表面相似可能误导，需要更主动地抽取原理、识别资源、提问和试验。迁移并非必然发生，也不能把一次成功或失败直接推广到所有场景。
moduleZh.reflection: 我现在坚持的哪个固定步骤，其实只是旧环境中的代理信号？换到新情境，我该先观察什么？

references.citation: Barnett, S. M., & Ceci, S. J. (2002). When and Where Do We Apply What We Learn? A Taxonomy for Far Transfer. Psychological Bulletin, 128(4), 612–637.
references.use: Defines transfer distance across content and context dimensions; cautions against treating far transfer as one uniform effect.

references.citation: Bransford, J. D., & Schwartz, D. L. (1999). Rethinking Transfer: A Simple Proposal With Multiple Implications. Review of Research in Education, 24, 61–100.
references.use: Frames transfer partly as preparation for future learning, not only immediate reproduction of prior performance.

references.citation: Perkins, D. N., & Salomon, G. (1992). Transfer of Learning. International Encyclopedia of Education, 2nd ed. Pergamon Press.
references.use: Explains positive/negative, near/far transfer and teaching strategies that connect contexts.

articles.title: The Silhouette Book Bound in Blue Thread
articles.summary: A flower-delivery apprentice who recognizes addresses quickly by the overall shape of whole words finds that the method does not transfer once the business routinely includes handwriting from many different people, and begins linking letters and sounds to meanings he already knows.
articles.summaryZh: 一名靠整词外形快速认地址的送花学徒，在业务固定包含多种手写订单后发现这种方法无法迁移，转而把字母、声音与已知词义连接起来。
storyParagraphs: The flower shop in the north of the city was entering wedding season, and Alo wanted to win a permanent delivery position for the winter. The owner’s condition was practical: for one month, no order could arrive late because Alo had misread an address. Alo spoke the local language and had heard most of the street names on his regular routes, but he had been learning its alphabet for less than half a year. To keep up with the work, he memorized common street names by their overall outlines: one looked like two pointed roofs, another ended in a long tail. He drew these “silhouettes” in a small notebook and tied it shut with blue thread. The shop’s printed labels used a fixed typeface, and he could often recognize them at a glance, much faster than sounding out each word.

For the first two weeks, the method genuinely worked. The signs downtown looked much like the shop’s labels, and Alo delivered quickly and accurately; soon even the urgent afternoon orders were being given to him. At the end of the month, the shop signed long-term contracts with four wedding venues. Each venue would write last-minute additions directly on cards and send them with different reception staff. This was not an exception but part of the new contract. On the first day, the handwriting on several cards still resembled print closely enough that Alo needed to add only two or three new silhouettes to his notebook and finished on time as usual. He tightened the blue thread by another notch.

On the third day, one card carried the name “Melo Lane,” a street Alo knew well by ear. The writer’s letters were thin and joined together, so the overall outline looked more like “Merlin Road” in his notebook. Alo chose the latter by shape, went two blocks out of his way, and arrived with the bouquet after the couple had already entered. The flower shop refunded the delivery fee. Back at the shop, Alo did not blame the handwriting. Instead, he found two other cards from that day that also said “Melo Lane.” Three people had written the same name, yet the three overall shapes barely resembled one another. Alo copied all three silhouettes into the notebook, and a single page was crowded at once.

That afternoon another unfamiliar handwritten order arrived. A second apprentice had never seen this customer’s handwriting, yet he pointed to several letters in the word, quietly joined their familiar sounds, and soon pronounced a street name Alo knew. Alo looked at the same card again. The paper had not become clearer, nor had the street become more familiar; only the lines he had treated as one solid shape now began to separate into internal positions. He stopped the pen he had been about to use for a fourth silhouette, broke the street name into the sounds he heard, and marked the corresponding letters beneath them one by one. The blue thread still held the old notebook together, but for the first time that page gained no new outline around a whole word.

Over the next few weeks, he read the same set of street names in different forms: the shop’s print, the joined handwriting of the four venues, and hurried notes from customers. With a familiar spoken word, he first listened for the sounds inside it, then looked for the corresponding letters; with a new word, he decoded it gradually from the parts he could identify. At first he slowed down noticeably, and several of the most urgent deliveries were assigned to someone else, costing him some commission. But after the same word had been read accurately a few times in different handwriting, Alo no longer needed to draw a new picture for every version. Some street names began to call up their familiar pronunciation and location as soon as they appeared.

The test for the permanent winter position was an order filled out on the spot by a customer whose handwriting Alo had never seen, and the address included a new street he had never delivered to. He read the opening sound first, joined the later letters to it, confirmed the district, and set out; he returned without asking anyone for help. Alo took the old silhouette notebook from his pocket and untied the blue thread. The “two pointed roofs” on the first page were still there. He did not tear them out. He only added small notes for letters and sounds beside them, then moved the blue thread from around the whole notebook to that page, where it served as a bookmark.
storyParagraphsZh: 城北花店进入婚礼旺季，阿洛想争到冬季的固定送货位。老板给他的条件很实际：一个月内，订单上的地址不能因为认错字而迟到。阿洛会说当地话，常跑的街名也大多听过，只是学习这套字母还不到半年。为了跟上工作，他把常见街名记成整体轮廓：有的像两座尖屋顶，有的末尾拖着长尾。他把这些“剪影”画进一本小册子，用蓝线捆住。店里的打印标签字体固定，他常常一眼就能认出，比逐字拼读快得多。
前两周，这套办法确实有效。市中心的路牌和店内标签样式接近，阿洛送得又快又准，午后的急单也开始交给他。月底花店接下四家婚礼场地的长期合作，场地方会把临时加单直接写在卡片上，由不同接待员随车送来；这不是例外，而是新合同的一部分。第一天的几张字迹还算接近印刷体，阿洛只需在剪影本里补两三个新轮廓，照样按时完成。他于是把蓝线又勒紧了一格。
第三天，一张卡片写着阿洛口头上很熟的“梅洛巷”。写单人的字母细长连在一起，整体轮廓和他本里的“梅林路”更像。阿洛按外形选了后者，多绕了两个街区，捧花送到时新人已经进场，花店退掉了配送费。回店后，他没有把责任推给笔迹，而是找到当天另外两张同样写着“梅洛巷”的卡片：三个人写的是同一个名字，三个整体形状却几乎不像。阿洛把三幅剪影都描进本子，一页立刻挤满。
下午又来一张陌生手写单。另一名学徒没见过这位客人的笔迹，却用手指点着词里的几个字母，低声把常见声音接起来，很快念出了阿洛认识的街名。阿洛拿过同一张卡片再看，纸没有变清楚，街道也没有变熟；只是那些原本被他当成一整团的线条，开始能分出内部位置。他停下准备画第四幅剪影的笔，把街名按听到的声音拆开，在下面逐个标出相应字母。蓝线仍捆着旧本，但那一页第一次没有新增整词外框。
接下来几周，他把同一批街名换着读：店内印刷体、四家场地的连笔、顾客匆忙写的便签。遇到熟悉的口语词，他先听清内部声音，再去找对应字母；遇到新词，就从能确定的部分逐步解码。最初明显慢下来，几单最急的配送被分给别人，他少拿了一些提成。但同一个词在不同笔迹里被准确读过几次后，阿洛不再需要为每一种写法新画一张图，有些街名甚至一出现就能连到原来的读音和地点。
冬季固定岗的测试是一张现场填写的订单，字迹来自阿洛从未见过的客人，地址里还有一条他没送过的新街名。他先读出开头的声音，再把后面的字母接上，确认路区后出门；回来时没有问过任何人。阿洛从口袋里掏出旧剪影本，解开蓝线。最上面那幅“两座屋顶”还在，他没有撕掉，只在旁边留下字母和声音的小记号，再把蓝线从整本外面绕到那一页做了书签。
explanationParagraphs: Orthographic mapping is the process by which a written word becomes stably linked in memory with its pronunciation and meaning. In alphabetic writing, readers use phonological awareness and letter-sound correspondences to decode words, and repeated accurate reading gradually supports automatic recognition. With practice, familiar words can then be recognized quickly. This differs from memorizing each whole word as one fixed visual picture.
explanationParagraphsZh: 正字法映射是书面词形与词语的发音、意义在记忆中建立稳定联系的过程。在字母文字中，读者依靠语音意识和字母—声音对应完成解码，并在反复准确识读后逐渐自动化，熟练后才能快速认词。它不同于把每个整词当成一幅固定图画死记。

module.intro: In alphabetic writing, rapid word recognition does not come from permanently memorizing each word as a picture, but from forming stable links among its internal spelling, sounds, and existing meaning.
module.diagramTitle: From Whole-Word Shape to Transferable Word Memory
diagramSteps: See a written word that needs to be read
Identify the letters and speech-sound units within it
Connect spelling, pronunciation, and an existing word meaning
Read the word accurately across different writing styles
Let familiar words gradually become fast and automatic to recognize
diagramStepNotes: Start with a real word that needs to be understood or spoken.
The key cues lie in internal correspondences, not only in the overall outline.
Existing spoken vocabulary allows the decoded sounds to connect with meaning.
Each accurate decoding strengthens a stable memory for the same word rather than storing a separate picture for every new typeface or handwriting style.
Once recognition becomes automatic, more attention can go to the address, sentence meaning, and real task.
mapping: The silhouette method is fast with fixed printed labels → Whole-word images can temporarily work in a stable environment
The same street name appears in three handwritten shapes → Overall outline does not transfer reliably
A coworker reads the same unfamiliar handwriting through letter sounds → Usable information is still present in the internal correspondences
Alo repeatedly decodes across different writing styles → Spelling, pronunciation, and location become increasingly linked
The blue thread changes from binding the whole book to marking one page → The old visual strategy is not erased, but it no longer carries the main burden of word recognition
module.boundary: This account concerns orthographic mapping in alphabetic writing and should not be used to assume that every writing system is learned in exactly the same way. Skilled reading also depends on more than one mechanism; vocabulary, language comprehension, and context matter as well. Overall visual features can support recognition, but they cannot replace stable internal letter-sound connections.
module.reflection: Why, by the time Alo drew a third silhouette for the same street, was the problem no longer simply “one more card is missing”?

moduleZh.intro: 在字母文字中，快速认词并不是把每个词永久记成一幅图，而是把内部字形、声音和已有意义建立稳定联系。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 从整词外形到可迁移的词形记忆
diagramSteps: 看见需要识读的书面词
辨认内部字母与语音单位
把拼写、读音和已有词义连接
在不同书写样式中反复准确识读
熟悉词逐渐实现快速自动识别
diagramStepNotes: 先有一个需要读懂或说出的真实词。
关键线索位于词的内部对应关系，而不只是整体轮廓。
已有口语词汇让解码出的声音能够接上意义。
每次准确解码都巩固同一词的稳定记忆，而不是为新字体另存一幅图。
自动化后，注意力可以更多用于地址、句意和实际任务。
mapping: 固定打印标签下剪影法很快 → 整词图像在稳定环境中可以暂时奏效
同一街名出现三种手写形状 → 整体轮廓无法稳定迁移
同事从同一张陌生笔迹中按字母读音识读 → 可用信息仍存在于内部对应关系
阿洛跨多种字体反复解码 → 拼写、读音与地点逐渐绑定
蓝线从捆整本改作书签 → 旧的图像策略没有被抹掉，但不再承担主要识读功能
moduleZh.boundary: 这里讨论的是字母文字中的正字法映射，不能简单推断所有书写系统都以完全相同方式学习。熟练阅读也不只依靠一种机制；词汇、语言理解和语境同样重要。整体视觉特征可以辅助识别，但不能替代稳定的内部字形—声音联系。
moduleZh.reflection: 为什么阿洛为同一条街画到第三幅剪影时，问题已经不再是“还差一张卡片”？

articles.title: Twelve Black Squares
articles.summary: As floodwater closes in on a granary, a porter first uses eighty and forty to define what is needed, then reorganizes loose sacks into checkable groups of five and ten so the boat can be loaded in time, with a final sack-by-sack count confirming the total.
articles.summaryZh: 洪水逼近粮仓时，一名搬运工先用八十加四十确定目标，再把散袋重组为五与十的可复核单位，为及时装船提供判断，并由最终逐袋点数确认。
storyParagraphs: When the storm drove the river up to the threshold of the South Granary, only one grain boat could still leave before the bridge opening closed. Its licence allowed no more than one hundred and twenty standard sacks of wheat; even one extra sack was too much to risk. Another half hour and the rising water would trap the boat on this side of the bridge. In the main store were eight rows of sacks sealed that morning, ten sacks to a row, with every seal intact. In the side room, however, lay loose sacks returned the night before, their number not yet entered in the ledger. Clerk Qiu’s pages had been blurred by the rain, and he decided to count the loose sacks one by one. Lan, one of the porters, knew an exact count was the safest answer. She also knew that the sacks nearest the door were already beginning to take on water.

The eight complete rows were moved first to dry ground, and their quantity was not in dispute: eighty sacks. The real question became how many more the boat could take, and how to select exactly that number from the irregular piles in the side room. Lan glanced inside and thought the two piles near the door looked like “about forty,” enough to load at once. Qiu shook his head immediately. The loose piles rose to different heights, and a boat licence could not rest on “about.” He began again with the first sack. Lan did not argue. By the time he reached seventeen, water had crossed the first brick joint in the side room.

The boatman coiled the second mooring line and warned them there was time for only one loading attempt. Lan looked at the eighty sacks already confirmed, crossed out eight squares on the loading board, and left four empty squares after them: one hundred and twenty minus eighty meant forty more. She stopped estimating whole piles. Instead, she dragged the loose sacks beside the scale platform in groups of five; only when two “fives” made a “ten” did she blacken one of the empty squares. The third group looked complete, but when the top burlap sack was moved, there were only four beneath it—the empty sack had puffed up just enough to suggest the shape of a fifth. Lan drew a short stroke beside the board and filled the group properly.

The side room soon held eight groups of five, paired into four groups of ten. Lan told the porters to carry only those forty sacks onto the boat and keep them separate from the first eight rows. In the end, the deck held twelve rows of ten. Qiu did not treat the grouping as the final ledger count, but he checked the twelve squares on the board, the loose sacks left in the side room, and the twelve rows on the boat. The three views of the quantity agreed, so on the temporary slip he signed, “Ship now; recount on arrival.” As the boatman cast off, the last black square had just been filled, and the water had reached the lowest rope in the side room.

The boat passed under the bridge with only a hand’s breadth between its gunwale and the stone arch. Six loose sacks left in the side room could not be raised in time and were later all damaged by water; that was the real cost of the earlier wait for a sack-by-sack recount. On higher ground, Qiu still counted from the first sack to the one hundred and twentieth. None was missing, and the boat had not been overloaded. He then checked once more by twelve rows of ten before entering the official total in the ledger. The group Lan had first misjudged was not erased from the record: beside the third square on the board, the short stroke showing “four sacks, not five” was still there.

After the flood receded, the South Granary made a new emergency loading board. Twelve large squares still represented one hundred and twenty sacks, and beside them were movable pieces for groups of five. Ordinary records were still kept sack by sack. Lan hung the old board behind the door. The first time a new porter asked what the short stroke meant, she did not rub it out. She simply paired eight “five-sack” pieces into four tens, then lined those four groups of ten up with the four black squares.
storyParagraphsZh: 暴雨把河水推到南仓门槛时，只剩一条粮船还能在桥洞关闭前离开。船证最多允许一百二十袋标准麦子，超一袋都不能冒险；再晚半个时辰，涨水又会把船挡在桥这边。主仓有八排早晨刚封过的麦袋，每排十袋，封签未动；侧屋却堆着昨晚退回的散袋，多少没有来得及入账。账房老邱的册页被雨打花，他决定先把散袋逐袋数清。搬运工小岚知道精确数最可靠，也知道门边的麦袋已经开始吸水。
八个完整排先被抬到干处，数量没有争议：八十袋。真正的问题变成船上还可以装多少，以及怎样从侧屋乱堆里取出恰好的数量。小岚朝侧屋看了一眼，觉得靠门两堆“差不多四十”，想先搬上船。老邱立刻摇头；散堆有高有低，船证不能靠“差不多”。他从第一袋开始重新点。小岚没有反驳。数到十七时，河水已漫进侧屋第一道砖缝。
船老大收起第二根缆绳，提醒只剩一次装船机会。小岚看着已经确认的八十袋，在装货木板上划掉八格，又在后面留下四个空格：一百二十减八十，还差四十。她不再估整堆，而是把散袋按五只一组拖到秤台边；两个“五”并成一个“十”，才涂黑一个空格。第三组看上去已经齐了，搬开最上面的麻包却只有四袋——那只空麻包正好撑出了第五袋的形状。小岚在木板旁划了一道短横，重新补足这一组。
侧屋很快排出八个“五”，两两合成四个“十”。小岚让搬运工只把这四十袋送上船，与先前八排分开摆；船面最终形成十二排，每排十袋。老邱没有把分组当成最终账目，但他重新看了一遍木板的十二格、侧屋留下的余袋和船上的十二排，三处数量能对上，便在临时单上签了“先运、到岸复点”。船老大解缆时，最后一个黑格刚涂满，水已经浸到侧屋最下面的麻绳。
船过桥洞时，船沿离石拱只剩一掌。留在侧屋的六袋散粮没能及时抬高，后来全部受潮；这是前面等待逐袋重数留下的现实代价。到了高岸，老邱仍从第一袋数到第一百二十袋，一袋不少，也没有超载。他又按十二排每排十袋复核一次，才把正式数字写回账上。小岚第一次看走眼的那一组并没有被抹掉：木板第三格旁，那道表示“四袋不是五袋”的短横还在。
洪水退后，南仓重新做了应急装运板。十二个大格仍代表一百二十袋，旁边增加了可以移动的“五袋”小片，平时的正式账目仍逐袋登记。小岚把旧木板挂在门后。新来的搬运工第一次问那道短横是什么意思时，她没有擦掉它，只把八个“五袋”小片两两并起，再把四组“十”依次对齐四个黑格。
explanationParagraphs: Number sense is a flexible understanding of quantity, magnitude, and numerical relationships. Benchmarks, grouping, decomposition, estimation, and multiple representations help a person judge what is plausible and choose an efficient calculation. Number sense does not replace exact counting when precision is required; it guides action and provides an independent way to check an answer. Estimation and exact calculation should verify one another.
explanationParagraphsZh: 数感是对数量、大小和数字关系的灵活理解。借助基准、分组、拆分、估计及不同表示方式，人能迅速判断结果是否合理，并选择有效算法。数感不替代需要时的精确计数；它为行动提供方向，也能用另一种方式核查答案，估计与精算应互相校验。

module.intro: Number sense helps a person first see the numerical relationships and plausible range, then choose efficient ways to group, decompose, and check; when precision is required, the process can still return to item-by-item confirmation.
module.diagramTitle: From Judging Numerical Relationships to Exact Confirmation
diagramSteps: Identify the target quantity and a known benchmark
Break the problem into easier numerical relationships
Use grouping or estimation to form an actionable quantity
Cross-check with a different representation
Complete an exact count when needed
diagramStepNotes: First clarify the limit, gap, or rough scale instead of immediately counting again from one.
Use the relationship between eighty and one hundred and twenty to turn the task into finding forty.
Familiar units such as five and ten reduce the cognitive load created by irregular piles.
The board squares, five-sack groups, and rows on the boat make the same quantity visible in different ways.
Exact counting provides the final confirmation; number sense does not remove the requirement for precision.
mapping: Eight sealed rows equal eighty sacks → Use a reliable benchmark instead of reconstructing the entire quantity from zero
One hundred and twenty minus eighty equals forty → Use the numerical relationship to narrow the real problem first
Loose sacks grouped by fives, with two groups joined into ten → Flexible regrouping is more checkable than judging a whole pile by sight
Twelve black squares compared with twelve rows on the boat → The same quantity is cross-checked through different representations
Every sack counted on arrival up to one hundred and twenty → Rapid judgment is still subject to exact verification
module.boundary: Number sense cannot replace procedures that require exact records, weighing, or auditing, nor can it turn a rough visual guess into a reliable answer. When items differ in size, the benchmark itself is unreliable, or the cost of error is extremely high, more direct measurement is needed. Its role is to help judge, organize, and check quantities, not to eliminate exact calculation.
module.reflection: When Lan truly changed her method, did she simply count faster, or did she first represent “how many more are needed” in a different way?

moduleZh.intro: 数感让人先看清数量关系和合理范围，再选择高效的分组、拆分与校验方式；需要精确时，最终仍可回到逐项确认。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 从数量关系判断到精确确认
diagramSteps: 确定目标数量与已知基准
把问题拆成更容易处理的数量关系
用分组或估计形成可行动的数量
换一种表示方式交叉校验
需要时完成精确计数确认
diagramStepNotes: 先弄清上限、缺口或大致规模，而不是立刻从一开始数。
利用八十与一百二十的关系，把任务转成寻找四十。
五、十等熟悉单位可以降低乱堆带来的认知负担。
木板格、五袋组和船上排布让同一数量从不同角度可见。
精确计数负责最后确认，数感并不取消精度要求。
mapping: 八排封签麦袋等于八十 → 使用可靠基准而非从零重建全部数量
一百二十减八十得四十 → 先利用数量关系缩小真正问题
散袋按五分组、两组并十 → 灵活重组比整堆目测更可复核
十二黑格与船上十二排对照 → 同一数量用不同表示交叉检查
到岸逐袋数到一百二十 → 快速判断最终仍接受精确验证
moduleZh.boundary: 数感不能替代必须精确记录、称量或审计的程序，也不能把粗略目测包装成可靠答案。当物品大小不一致、基准本身不可信或误差代价极高时，需要更直接的测量。它的作用是帮助判断、组织和校验数量，而不是取消精算。
moduleZh.reflection: 小岚真正改变方法的那一刻，是她更快地“数”了，还是先把“还差多少”重新表示了？

articles.title: A Fold Showing Only Q7
articles.summary: A printer who can accurately proofread and read aloud an entire fuel notice still fails when he must actually collect supplies because he does not connect the district code, date, depot, time slot, and required documents into an action, until he changes the way he uses the document.
articles.summaryZh: 一名能准确校读并朗读整张燃料告示的印刷工，在真正代领物资时却没有把街区代码、日期、仓库、时段与凭证连成行动，直到他改变使用文件的方式。
storyParagraphs: Before the cold wave arrived, the boiler room at Stonebridge Apartments had only one night of coal left. City Hall had just issued a temporary fuel-rationing table, and the building manager asked Luo Cheng, who worked at the print shop, to collect their allocation because he had proofread that very table the night before. District codes, dates, depots, time slots, required documents—he had checked every word and had even caught a missing digit. Luo Cheng normally read contracts and official notices without stumbling, and his handwriting was elegant. But this time reading the words correctly was not enough. Twenty-two households of elderly people and children would still need heat the following night; if the coal was not collected, the building would have to use its repair fund to buy expensive loose coal.

The official notice was a wide table. District codes ran down the left side, dates across the top, followed by the collection depot, time, required documents, and household quota. Luo Cheng read the whole table aloud again from beginning to end and knew every word. Stonebridge Apartments was in the north of the city. When he saw the prominent words “North Depot,” he circled them on his copy. The “Q7” printed in the corner of the building’s coal certificate was also easy for him to read, but he never used it to locate the corresponding row. While he waited, a building manager ahead of him checked the code on her certificate, ran one finger across the Q6 row, and quickly moved to another vehicle. Luo Cheng stayed at the end of the North Depot queue.

At the window, the clerk checked his coal certificate and turned the original notice toward him: for Q7 that day, the table specified West Depot, from fourteen hundred to fifteen hundred, together with the current month’s resident list and the apartment seal. Luo Cheng had brought last month’s list. He hurried back to exchange the document, then rode to West Depot, only to see the iron gate close in front of him. The depot had not cancelled Stonebridge’s allocation, and the staff had added no new condition. The day’s vehicles for each district had already been loaded according to the table, so they could not take coal from another district’s share for twenty-two households. The manager had to use the repair fund to buy two cartloads of loose coal to get through the next two nights. Every word Luo Cheng had proofread the night before was still printed on the page exactly as it had been.

On the third day, City Hall issued a make-up collection schedule in exactly the same format. Luo Cheng placed the coal certificate against the left side of the notice, aligned its Q7 with Q7 in the table, then traced across that single row through the date, West Depot, collection period, current month’s resident list, apartment seal, and twenty-two households. He did not copy the whole notice. Instead, he placed a small black dot beneath each item that had to be acted on. Then he folded the paper so that every other district disappeared behind it and only the Q7 row remained visible. When the manager took it, she needed only to check that one row against the documents on the table. The earlier copy, neatly filled from edge to edge, still lay beside it. This time it had nothing to do.

On the afternoon of the make-up collection, Luo Cheng arrived at West Depot early with the current month’s resident list and the apartment seal. The window checked the quota for twenty-two households, exchanged the coal voucher for a loading slip, and asked for nothing else. Back at the print shop, Luo Cheng still proofread complete texts. But when he handled a delivery note, he checked the order number, address, and deadline on the same line; when printing pharmacy pickup slips, he checked that the name, date, and dosage instructions had not been placed in the wrong fields. His reading fluency had not changed, nor had his neat handwriting. What changed was that the information on the page began to be connected around the task it was meant to support.

The night the new coal reached Stonebridge Apartments, the manager tipped the first shovelful into the boiler. Luo Cheng folded the make-up notice into a small square and slipped it into the boiler-room ledger folder with only the Q7 row showing. His first copy, with the entire notice written out neatly, remained behind it. The new crease ran through the middle of the page, exactly across the two words “North Depot” that he had circled the first time.
storyParagraphsZh: 寒潮来临前，石桥公寓的锅炉房只剩一晚煤。市政厅刚发布临时燃料配给表，管理员请印刷铺的罗成代领，因为那张表的校样正是他昨晚检查过的：街区代码、日期、仓库、时段、凭证，他逐字看过，还改出一个漏印的数字。罗成平日读合同和公文从不卡顿，字也写得漂亮。可这次事情不能只读准——二十二户老人和孩子第二晚还要取暖，若领不到，公寓就得动用维修金买高价散煤。
正式告示是一张横向表格。左边列街区代码，上面分日期，后面依次是领取仓库、时间、所需清单和户数配额。罗成把整张表又从头到尾念了一遍，所有词都认识。石桥公寓在城北，他看到表中醒目的“北仓”，便在自己的抄本上把这两个字圈了起来；至于公寓煤证角落里的“Q7”，他也读得出，却没有拿它去找对应那一行。排队时，前面一位管理员先看煤证代码，再用手指横着扫过Q6那行，很快转去另一辆车。罗成仍留在北仓队尾。
轮到窗口，工作人员核对煤证后把原告示转向他：Q7当天对应的是西仓，十四时到十五时，并要求本月住户清单和公寓章。罗成带来的清单是上月的。他赶回去换文件，再坐车去西仓，铁门在他前面合上。仓库没有取消石桥公寓的配额，工作人员也没有额外加条件；当天各街区的车已经按表装完，不能从别人的份额里临时拆二十二户。管理员只得用维修金买两车散煤，先撑过两夜。罗成昨晚校过的每一个字，此刻仍原样印在纸上。
第三天，市政厅发布补领安排，格式和上一张完全一样。罗成把煤证压在告示左边，让Q7与表格中的Q7对齐，再沿这一行横着划过日期、西仓、领取时段、当月清单、公寓章和二十二户。他没有抄全文，只在每个要执行的项目下面点一个小黑点。随后把纸折起，其他街区全部藏到背面，只露出Q7这一条；管理员拿过来，只需核对这一行和桌上的材料。原来写满整页的抄本还在旁边，这次却没有派上用场。
补领日的下午，罗成提前到了西仓，带着本月清单和公寓章。窗口按二十二户核完配额，煤票换成装车单，没有补问任何材料。之后回到印刷铺，他仍负责校读整篇文字，但遇到送货单时会把订单号、地址和截止时间放在同一行核；替药店印取药凭条时，会确认姓名、日期和剂量说明有没有被分到错误栏位。朗读能力没有改变，漂亮字也没有变，变化只是纸上的信息开始按实际任务重新连在一起。
新煤送到石桥公寓那晚，管理员把第一铲倒进锅炉。罗成将补领告示折成一小块，夹进锅炉房账夹，只露出Q7那一行。最初那份抄得整整齐齐的全文仍留在后面。新的折痕从纸中央穿过，正好压住他第一次圈起来的“北仓”两个字。
explanationParagraphs: Functional literacy is the ability to understand and use written language, numbers, tables, and symbols to complete real tasks. It includes locating relevant information, recognizing a document’s purpose, combining conditions, and checking a decision, as well as adjusting the way one reads to the task. Fluent reading aloud or elegant handwriting alone does not ensure that a person can use a timetable, form, contract, or set of instructions.
explanationParagraphsZh: 功能性读写能力是理解并使用文字、数字、表格和符号完成现实任务的能力，包括定位相关信息、识别文件用途、组合条件并核查决定，还需要依任务调整阅读方式。朗读流利或书写漂亮，并不保证一个人会使用时刻表、表单、合同或操作说明。

module.intro: Functional literacy is not only about whether someone can read the words; it also concerns whether they can find, combine, and use the information relevant to a real task.
module.diagramTitle: From Reading the Words to Using Them to Complete a Task
diagramSteps: Clarify the real task and the relevant object first
Locate the text or fields relevant to the task
Integrate dates, conditions, quantities, and the relevant object
Act on the integrated information
Check the interpretation again against the result and the document
diagramStepNotes: In the same document, only part of the content is usually directly relevant to the current task.
Tables, codes, symbols, and notes may all determine where to look.
Understanding is not recognizing each item separately, but connecting distributed fields into a set of conditions that can be acted on.
Functional literacy becomes visible in decisions such as where to go, when to go, what to bring, and how much to do.
If the action fails, return to the relationship between the information and the task rather than simply rereading the whole document.
mapping: Luo Cheng had already caught a missing printed digit → Basic word recognition and line-by-line accuracy are not the main gap
The Q7 on the coal certificate is not aligned with Q7 in the table → Information that was read is not located for the current case
Seeing “North Depot” and acting on geographic intuition → One prominent phrase replaces integration across fields
The folded notice shows only the Q7 row, with each required item dotted → The document is reorganized into executable conditions
The crease runs through “North Depot” → The same phrase changes from a dominant cue into information that must be understood within its row-and-column relationships
module.boundary: Functional literacy should not turn every failure into an individual deficit. If a document is badly designed, information is missing, the language is unsuitable, or rules change without warning, even a highly capable reader may fail. This story deliberately keeps the same table complete and the rules stable so that the focus remains on how readable information is turned into action.
module.reflection: Luo Cheng had already “read” Q7, West Depot, and the collection time the first time. Why did those correct words still fail to form the correct action?

moduleZh.intro: 功能性读写关注的不只是“能不能读出字”，还包括能否从真实文件中找到、组合并使用与任务有关的信息。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 从读到文字到用文字完成任务
diagramSteps: 先明确现实任务和对象
定位与任务相关的文本或字段
把日期、条件、数量和对象整合起来
依据整合后的信息采取行动
用结果和文件再次核查理解
diagramStepNotes: 同一份文件里通常只有一部分内容与当前任务直接相关。
表格、代码、符号和注释都可能决定该看哪里。
理解不是逐项认字，而是把分散字段连成一个可执行条件组合。
真正的读写能力会落到去哪、何时去、带什么、做多少等决定。
若行动失败，应回到信息与任务的对应关系检查，而不只是重读全文。
mapping: 罗成曾校出漏印数字 → 基础识字和逐字准确性不是主要缺口
煤证Q7没有与表格Q7对齐 → 已读信息没有被定位到当前对象
看到“北仓”便据地理常识行动 → 单个醒目词取代了跨字段整合
折叠后只露Q7一行并逐项点记 → 文本被重新组织为可执行条件
折痕压过“北仓” → 同一个词从主导行动的线索变成必须置于行列关系中理解的信息
moduleZh.boundary: 功能性读写不能把所有失败都归给个人。若文件本身设计混乱、信息缺失、语言不适配或规则临时改变，即使能力很强也可能出错。本故事刻意让同一张表信息完整、规则稳定，讨论的是如何把可读信息转化为行动。
moduleZh.reflection: 罗成第一次其实已经“读过”Q7、西仓和领取时段，为什么这些正确的字仍没有组成正确的行动？

articles.title: Forty Minutes Behind the Badge
articles.summary: A trainee museum guide discovers that her repeated overruns are not caused by an overly long script, but by turning the feeling that “the visitors may not have understood” directly into more explanation—until predictions, evidence, and checkpoints begin to change what she does next.
articles.summaryZh: 一名博物馆见习讲解员发现，反复超时并不是因为讲稿太长，而是她总把“观众可能没听懂”的感觉直接变成继续解释；直到她让预测、证据和检查点真正改变下一步动作。
storyParagraphs: Ninglan had only two guided-tour evaluations left. If she passed, she would stay on the National Day holiday roster; if she failed once more, those holiday hours would go to someone else. The museum’s blue route card was always tucked behind her badge, with the latest departure time printed for each of the five galleries. On her first formal tour, she was only a minute or two late through the first two galleries, but at the cracked celadon bowl she spoke for seven minutes longer than planned. By the time the last six visitors reached the restoration workshop, the staff had already begun putting away the tools. Ninglan thought the problem was that she spoke too slowly when nervous, so she cut nearly a third of her script and practised each section until it flowed more smoothly.

The second rehearsal took place after closing, with no visitors to ask questions and only one colleague following with a stopwatch. Ninglan was even ahead of the blue card through the first two galleries, yet at the celadon bowl she was still six minutes late. She had no extra stories left to cut, but she fell behind again in the mural gallery. Back in the office, she stopped editing the script. Instead, she drew three columns on the back of the blue card: planned departure time, actual departure time, and how certain she had felt that “the listeners had understood.” During the next two empty-gallery rehearsals, she kept the same record and added a small dot whenever she inserted an unplanned sentence.

When she laid the cards side by side, the delays did not always occur in the same places, but the small dots consistently clustered beside moments of low certainty. If someone frowned, failed to nod, or if a causal link still felt incomplete to her, she would add another example; then she would worry that the transition no longer connected and add one more sentence. Each addition was reasonable on its own and took only tens of seconds, yet even after the time printed on the blue card had passed, she often told herself she could make it up in the next gallery. Ninglan crossed out “speak faster” and replaced it with two actions: when the time was up, first check understanding; if one question could verify it, do not add an explanation first. If the actual time was two minutes behind, keep only essential information in the next section.

Twelve visitors came for the final evaluation. A family of three fell behind in the first gallery, and at the celadon bowl the child asked a question that was not in Ninglan’s script. She touched the badge at her chest; the blue card showed that she was already two minutes late. Instead of telling both of the stories she had prepared, she asked the child why the crack had not been filled in. The child pointed to the restoration photograph beside the case and said it was a trace left later. Ninglan added one sentence and moved the group on. In the fourth gallery, she crossed out a section of collection history that was optional. By the next doorway, the second hand had moved back close to the time printed on the card.

In front of the final mural, a visitor suddenly asked what year the work had entered the collection. Ninglan remembered two similar dates but was not certain which one was correct. In the past, she would have started again from the earlier history, talking while she searched for the answer she trusted more. This time she simply placed a black dot in the corner of the blue card, noted that she would verify it after the tour, and continued with what she could confirm. The evaluator neither rescued her nor hurried her. When they reached the restoration workshop, the staff had just set out twelve pairs of gloves, and all three members of the family had made it inside.

Only after handing the visitors over did Ninglan turn over the blue card behind her badge: two minutes late leaving the third gallery, one minute and twenty seconds recovered in the fourth, final time thirty-nine minutes and forty-six seconds. Before the visitors dispersed, she went back to check the year and wrote the answer beside the black dot. The bottom of the card had been blank. She added one line: “What should I check first next time?” Then she tucked the card behind her badge again.
storyParagraphsZh: 宁岚只剩两次带团考核。通过，她就能留在国庆排班里；再失败一次，假期那几天的工时便会给别人。馆方的蓝色路线卡一直夹在她胸牌后面，五个展厅各印着最晚离场时间。第一次正式带团，她在前两厅都只慢了一两分钟，却在那只裂纹青瓷碗前多讲了七分钟，最后六位游客赶到修复体验室时，工作人员已经开始收工具。宁岚以为问题是自己紧张时说得太慢，回去删掉近三分之一讲稿，又把每段练到更顺。
第二次彩排安排在闭馆后，没有游客提问，一名同事只拿秒表跟在后面。宁岚前两厅甚至比蓝卡快，到了青瓷碗前仍晚了六分钟。她已经没有多余故事可删，却又在壁画厅迟了一次。回办公室后，她没再改讲稿，而是在蓝卡背面画三栏：原定离场时间、实际离场时间、当时自己有多确定“听的人已经明白”。接下来的两次空馆练习，她照样记录，连自己临时补过的句子也在旁边点一个小圆点。

几张卡摊在一起后，迟到的位置并不完全相同，小圆点却总挤在低把握度那一栏旁边。有人皱眉、没有点头，或她自己觉得某个因果还没讲圆，她就会补一个例子；补完又担心前后没接上，再补一句。那些追加内容每次都合理，单独看也只占几十秒，可一旦蓝卡上的时间已经过去，她仍常告诉自己下一厅可以追回来。宁岚把“讲快一点”划掉，改写两条动作：到点先检查理解；能用一个问题验证的，不先追加解释。若实际时间落后两分钟，下一段只保留必讲信息。
最后一次考核来了十二位游客。一家三口在第一厅就落后，孩子到了青瓷碗前又问了一个讲稿里没有的问题。宁岚摸到胸牌，蓝卡显示已经晚两分钟。她没有把准备过的两个故事都拿出来，只问孩子为什么这道裂纹没有被补平。孩子指向旁边的修复照片，说那是后来留下的痕迹。宁岚补了一句便带队离开，在第四厅把一段可讲可不讲的收藏史划掉。走到下一个门口时，秒针重新落回蓝卡印着的时间附近。
最后一幅壁画前，一位游客忽然问到作品入藏的年份。宁岚记得两个相近数字，却没有足够把握。过去她会从前史重新讲起，边讲边寻找自己更相信的那个答案；这次她只在蓝卡角上点了一个黑点，记下展后核实，随后继续讲能够确认的部分。考核员没有替她解围，也没有催促。到修复室门口时，工作人员刚把十二副手套摆上桌，那一家三口也全都跟了进来。
把游客交过去后，宁岚才翻开胸牌后的蓝卡：第三厅晚两分钟，第四厅追回一分二十秒，最终用时三十九分四十六秒。游客散场前，她又回去查了那个年份，把答案写在黑点旁边。蓝卡最下方原本空着，她添了一行：“下次最先检查什么？”随后把卡片重新夹回胸牌后面。
explanationParagraphs: Metacognitive regulation involves planning an approach, monitoring understanding or progress, evaluating evidence and results, and adjusting strategy accordingly. Confidence, confusion, predictions, and outcomes become useful only when they inform the next action. It is not endless self-analysis, but a timely check on whether the current method is working and a prior decision about how to change when it is not.
explanationParagraphsZh: 元认知调节包括计划方法、监控理解或进展、评价证据与结果，并据此调整策略。信心、困惑、预测和结果只有进入下一步行动才有价值。它不是无休止地分析自己，而是在关键时刻检查当前方法是否有效，并预先决定无效时怎样改变。

module.intro: Effective self-monitoring is not thinking something through one more time; it is letting predictions, feedback, and deviations change the next strategy in time.
module.diagramTitle: The regulation cycle from planning to adjustment
diagramSteps: Set the goal and approach
Predict and set checkpoints
Monitor real-world feedback
Compare results with expectations
Adjust the strategy and continue
diagramStepNotes: First clarify what needs to be completed and what approach will be used to move forward.
Turn progress into observable signals such as time, results, or signs of understanding.
Record both external outcomes and internal states such as confidence or confusion.
Identify where the deviation comes from instead of treating every failure as a lack of effort.
Use pre-set or newly formed rules to change the next action, then expose the new strategy to further feedback.
mapping: The blue route card behind the badge originally showed only departure times → Having a plan does not mean the plan is being used to regulate action.
Even after shortening the script, the empty-gallery rehearsal still ran late in different places → Simply speaking faster or cutting content cannot explain the problem.
Actual time, confidence, and unplanned additions were recorded on the same card → Subjective judgment and objective progress became comparable.
Check understanding when time is up; if two minutes behind, remove nonessential content → Monitoring information began to trigger specific control actions.
The final time was thirty-nine minutes and forty-six seconds, followed by “What should I check first next time?” → One successful attempt still feeds into the next cycle of planning and monitoring.
module.boundary: Metacognitive regulation cannot replace professional knowledge, real skill, or reliable information. Poorly designed checkpoints or limited feedback can also mislead; in highly automated or extremely time-pressured tasks, excessive self-monitoring may consume attention.
module.reflection: If Ninglan had noticed only that “I ran over time again,” without comparing her judgment at the time with the actual result, what would she most likely have kept changing?

moduleZh.intro: 真正有效的自我监控，不是多想一遍，而是让预测、反馈和偏差及时改变下一步策略。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 从计划到调整的调节循环
diagramSteps: 设定目标与方法
预测并设置检查点
监控现实反馈
比较结果与预期
调整策略并继续
diagramStepNotes: 先明确要完成什么，以及准备用什么方法推进。
把进度变成可观察的时间、结果或理解信号。
同时记录外部结果和自己的把握、困惑等状态。

articles.title: Before the Green Light Comes On
articles.summary: A trainee station worker who already has the basic skills for announcements but keeps avoiding the real microphone gradually updates her judgment of “Can I finish this live?” through a series of verifiable on-the-job completions.
articles.summaryZh: 一名已经具备播报基本技能、却总避开真实麦克风的见习站务员，通过一系列可核验的现场完成记录，逐步更新自己对“我能不能在现场把它做完”的判断。
storyParagraphs: Yunan’s temporary contract had only three weeks left. To become a permanent station worker, she had to complete two live announcements independently during her final assessment shift. Six months earlier, the first time she used the microphone, her mind had gone blank after the words “Platform Two.” She fell silent for several seconds until the shift supervisor took over. Since then, she had always volunteered for ticket checks and passenger questions, leaving shifts that required announcements to someone else. Yet she continued to pass every weekly studio assessment: the same two announcement formats, the same train and platform information, and even the restart phrasing under simulated crowd noise had never caused a problem. The difficulty appeared only when the green indicator light on the real control desk came on.

The shift supervisor stopped letting colleagues take turns telling her to “relax.” He clipped a small record card beside the control desk and first had Yunan make a cleaning announcement on an empty platform after closing. She completed it and wrote down the date herself. Two days later, during a quieter midday period, she made a routine platform-change announcement and completed that as well. On the third attempt, a new platform number came through her headset before it had been confirmed. She did not guess. She stopped and asked dispatch to verify it before she announced anything. The card did not say “failure.” It recorded only the task, whether it was completed, and whether any incorrect information had been broadcast.

The fourth task was still the platform-change announcement she had long known, except that it was moved to the evening; the fifth used the same wording, but with more waiting passengers and louder background noise. Before each live announcement, Yunan wrote at the edge of the card how likely she thought she was to complete it, then recorded the result afterward. On the first three she had written only four or five out of ten, yet she completed them in succession; even the deliberate stop had produced no incorrect announcement. After the fifth task, she looked at the row of “completed” entries and the single “information unconfirmed—stopped.” For the first time, she did not wait for the supervisor to assign her. She wrote her own name beside a short rush-hour announcement for the next day.

On the afternoon of the permanent-post assessment, a fault on a neighbouring line turned the two routine notices into an unexpected platform change. The concourse was noisy, and the queue stretched to the stairs. Under the rules, the shift supervisor could simply make the announcement himself, while Yunan would have to wait for the next assessment round. Her palm was still damp when she reached for the microphone, and her fingers paused at the edge of its base. The record card lay beneath them: five completed tasks, one deliberate stop because information was unconfirmed, zero incorrect announcements. She pushed the card aside and drew the microphone toward her.

When the green indicator light came on, the first sentence was smooth. Halfway through the second, just as she reached the destination, a passenger beside the booth tapped on the glass with a question. Yunan paused for two seconds, and the sentence she had been saying disappeared from her mind. She did not hand the microphone back. Instead, she used the restart phrasing she had already mastered in the studio and announced the train, destination, and new platform again. The crowd began to move. After she finished, dispatch added a door-opening direction. Yunan waited for it to appear on the screen, then opened the microphone a second time and gave the additional information separately. The shift supervisor only ticked two boxes on the assessment sheet.

Yunan received a permanent place on the roster. Before her first announcement the next morning, she still checked the script, and she did not claim that she would never feel nervous again. When the green light came on, she did not look toward the shift supervisor. Instead, she turned the record card over, ready to log the next task. The final line on the front read: six completed, one deliberate stop, zero incorrect announcements.
storyParagraphsZh: 余南的临时合同只剩三周。想转成正式站务员，她必须在最后一次考核班次里独立完成两条现场播报。半年前第一次上麦时，她说到“二号站台”后突然脑中一片空白，沉默了几秒，最后由值班长接过话筒。从那以后，她总主动去做检票和问询，把需要上麦的班次让给别人。可每周的录音室考核她一直合格：同样的两套通知格式、同样的车次与站台信息，连模拟人群噪声下的重启句式也从未出错。问题只在控制台那盏绿色指示灯真正亮起时。
值班长不再让同事轮流劝她“放轻松”。他在控制台旁夹了一张小记录卡，先让余南在闭站后的空站台播一条清洁通知。她完成后，自己写下日期。两天后，她在午间客流较少时播普通换台通知，也完整说完。第三次耳机里临时传来一个尚未确认的新站台号，她没有猜，直接停下，请调度核实后再播。卡上没有写“失败”，只记了任务、是否完成，以及有没有播出错误信息。
第四次仍是她早已练熟的换台通知，只把时段移到傍晚；第五次也是同样的句式，只是候车的人更多、背景更吵。余南每次上麦前都在卡边写一个自己估计的完成把握，播完再记结果。前三次她都只写四成或五成，却连续完成；那次主动停止也没有造成错误广播。第五次结束后，她盯着一排“完成”和一个“信息未确认，停止”，第一次没有等值班长分配，主动把第二天晚高峰的一条短通知写到自己名字下面。
转正考核那天下午，邻线故障，原本两次例行通知变成临时换台。大厅里很吵，队伍排到楼梯口。按规定，值班长可以直接代播，余南则只能等下一轮考核。她伸手拿话筒时掌心仍发凉，手指在底座边停了一下。记录卡正压在那里：五次完成，一次因信息未确认主动停止，错误播出零次。她把卡往旁边推开，拉过话筒。
绿色指示灯亮起后，第一句很顺。第二句刚说到目的地，旁边一名乘客敲玻璃询问，余南停了两秒，原来的句子从脑中断掉。她没有把话筒递回去，而是用自己在录音室早已会的重启句式，重新报车次、目的地和新站台。人群开始移动。播完后，调度又追加一个车门方向，她先等屏幕确认，再第二次开麦，把补充内容单独说完。值班长只在考核表上勾了两个格。
余南拿到了正式排班。第二天清晨第一条播报前，她仍先核对稿子，也没有说自己以后不会紧张。绿灯亮起时，她没有去看值班长，而是把记录卡翻到背面，准备记下一次任务。正面最后一行是：完成六次，主动停止一次，错误播出零次。
explanationParagraphs: Self-efficacy is a person’s belief that they can organise and carry out the actions required for a particular task. It influences choice, effort, persistence, and recovery after setbacks. It is not general confidence and cannot replace real competence. Gradually accumulated mastery experiences, suitable modelling, feedback, and interpretations of stress can provide evidence for that belief.
explanationParagraphsZh: 自我效能感是人对自己能否组织并完成某项具体任务所需行动的信念，会影响选择、努力、坚持和受挫后的恢复。它不等于泛泛自信，也不能替代真实能力。逐步获得的成功经验、合适示范、反馈以及对紧张反应的解释，能为这种信念提供依据。

module.intro: Whether a person starts, and whether they continue after difficulty, often depends on their judgment of whether they can complete this specific task.
module.diagramTitle: Updating self-efficacy in a specific task
diagramSteps: Face a specific task
Form a judgment about completion
Choose whether to engage and persist
Gain credible evidence from results
Update the judgment and take on the next step
diagramStepNotes: The judgment should concern a specific task, not a broad question of whether “I am capable.”
Past experience, feedback, and current state all influence the perceived likelihood of success.
That judgment affects whether a person starts, how much they invest, and whether they continue when they get stuck.
Real completion, appropriate withdrawal, and clear feedback all provide new evidence about capability.
Once the judgment is updated, a person may be willing to take on a more demanding but still feasible task.
mapping: She consistently passed studio assessments but kept giving real microphone shifts to others → Basic skill and belief about a specific task can be out of sync.
Live tasks began with simple announcements during low-traffic periods → Manageable but real tasks provided credible mastery experiences.
One deliberate stop because information was unconfirmed, with zero incorrect announcements → Self-efficacy is not bravado; a correct withdrawal can also calibrate judgment.
After five consecutive live results, she volunteered for a rush-hour announcement → New evidence changed her choice and level of engagement.
After a brief lapse during the assessment, she continued with a restart phrase she had already mastered → The change appeared in persistence and recovery, not merely in learning a new technique.
module.boundary: Self-efficacy cannot create skills that do not exist, nor can it remove equipment failures, incorrect information, or real danger. Excessive and poorly calibrated confidence can also lead to bad choices, so mastery evidence should be considered together with actual competence, feedback, and task difficulty.
module.reflection: What truly changed for Yunan: whether she knew how to make the announcement, or how she judged her ability to carry out what she already knew in a real setting?

moduleZh.intro: 人是否愿意开始、遇阻后是否继续，常取决于他对自己能否完成这项具体任务的判断。
moduleZh.diagramTitle: 具体任务中的自我效能更新
diagramSteps: 面对具体任务
形成完成判断
选择是否投入与坚持
从结果获得可信证据
更新判断并承担下一步
diagramStepNotes: 判断必须针对具体任务，而不是笼统的“我行不行”。
过去经历、反馈和当下状态都会影响对成功可能性的判断。
这种判断会影响是否开始、投入多少以及卡住后是否继续。
真实完成、合理退出和明确反馈都会提供新的能力证据。
判断被更新后，人可能愿意承担更高一级但仍可行的任务。
mapping: 录音室考核长期合格，却总把真实上麦班次让给别人 → 基本技能与具体任务信念可以不同步。
低客流现场从简单通知开始 → 可完成但真实的任务提供可信掌握经验。
一次因信息未确认主动停止且零错误 → 自我效能不是逞强，正确退出也能校准判断。
连续五次现场结果后主动认领晚高峰通知 → 新证据改变了她的选择与投入。
考核中短暂断句后继续使用早已掌握的重启句式 → 变化体现在受挫后的坚持与恢复，而不只是新学会技巧。
moduleZh.boundary: 自我效能感不能创造不存在的技能，也不能消除设备故障、错误信息或真实危险。过高而失准的信心同样可能带来错误选择，因此可信经验应与实际能力、反馈和任务难度一起判断。
moduleZh.reflection: 余南真正改变的，是她会不会播，还是她如何判断自己在真实现场能不能把已经会的动作做完？
